label: active liquidity market
summary: Plan an orderbook, bin, vault, or inventory-driven market inside one custom v4 hook with a dedicated executable quoter and explicit liveness.
requiredFacts: Exact pricing, spread, bin or order rules; inventory and share math; deposits, withdrawals, fees and loss allocation
Dedicated quote path that executes the same hook state transition, sender, hookData, price limits and partial-fill behavior as swaps
Vault and PoolId namespace, ownership, maker permissions, cancellation, JIT or lock rules, and solvency invariants
Keeper or maker liveness assumptions, stale inventory, unavailable quote source, fallback and user exit
How mandatory Programmable fees compose with market spreads, LP fees, maker fees and project charges without double counting
requiredFiles: Pricing and inventory specification with worked examples
Pinned hook, vault, quoter and client source closure
Maker, keeper, custody, cancellation and exit authority map
Executable stateful invariants and adversarial market simulations
App quote, route, disclosure and monitoring integration
requiredTests: All swap quadrants, partial fills, depleted inventory, crossed or empty book, boundary bins, rounding and price limits
Quote-to-execution parity under same-block state change, maker action, JIT behavior, hookData change and reorg
Deposit, withdrawal, share donation, loss, cancellation, expiry, lock, unauthorized maker and cross-pool isolation
Keeper or quoter outage, stale state, gas exhaustion, reentrancy, malicious token and recovery
Fee composition, liabilities, claims, solvency, user exit and retirement after every successful and reverting path
risks: Custom market math creates a larger invariant and manipulation surface than an ordinary concentrated-liquidity pool
A non-equivalent quoter can present executable-looking prices that the hook cannot or will not honor
Inventory, vault shares, maker orders and PoolManager deltas can diverge unless one state machine owns settlement
